summary: Apple requires developers to be an Account Holder in the Apple Developer Program and to submit a request form to join the Mini Apps Partner Program. After testing, the app binary and a generic mini‑app In‑App Purchase Product ID must be submitted via App Store Connect, and the app must have access to the Advanced Commerce API (which may require an additional request). steps.title: Create a Services ID (OAuth client) in App Store Connect
steps.detail: Log into App Store Connect, go to **Identifiers → Services IDs**, click the “+” button, and create a new Services ID for your app.
steps.where: App Store Connect > Identifiers > Services IDs

steps.title: Configure the Services ID for Sign in with Apple
steps.detail: Give the Services ID a name, enable **Sign in with Apple**, and add your app’s redirect URI(s) under the **Web Authentication Configuration** section.
steps.where: App Store Connect > Identifiers > Services IDs > <your Services ID>

steps.title: Submit your app binary and Mini App In‑App Purchase product ID
steps.detail: After testing, upload your app binary and the generic Mini App In‑App Purchase Product ID through App Store Connect.
steps.where: App Store Connect > My Apps > <your app>

nuances.title: Redirect URI restrictions
nuances.detail: Apple only accepts HTTPS redirect URIs that exactly match the values entered in the Services ID configuration; wildcards or non‑HTTPS schemes are rejected during token exchange.

nuances.title: Sandbox vs. Production credentials
nuances.detail: Credentials generated in the sandbox environment (used for testing) are separate from production credentials; you must switch to production after your app passes review.
